findings: Low limb lead voltage with poor R progression

echoTasks.find: Dilated left ventricle with globally reduced thickening
Functional mitral regurgitation from annular dilatation with a dilated left atrium
Preserved pleural sliding without B lines on lung views

auscultation.murmur: Soft pansystolic murmur of functional mitral regurgitation at the apex

exam.general: Young man, breathless at rest, cool hands, mild ankle oedema to mid shin
exam.jvp: Raised 7 cm with prominent v waves
exam.other: Liver palpable 2 cm, bibasal crackles to mid zones, no wheeze
exam.precordium: Displaced diffuse apex beat in the sixth space outside the midclavicular line
exam.pulse: Tachycardic 92, low volume, regular, narrow pulse pressure

history.a: High fever with body ache diagnosed as dengue two months ago, breathlessness since recovery, now NYHA class III
history.q: Fever history and onset of breathlessness

history.a: Yes, wakes gasping twice a week, uses three pillows
Swelling of both feet by evening for three weeks, weight up 4 kg
No chest pain, occasional palpitation, no syncope
No alcohol, no smoking, no known heart disease, no family deaths at young age
Auto driver, off work for a month, worried about EMIs

keyPoints: Admit for decongestion with furosemide 40 mg intravenously for pulmonary oedema, per the ESC heart failure guideline
Start guideline directed therapy stepwise with an ACE inhibitor, beta blocker, mineralocorticoid antagonist and SGLT2 inhibitor once euvolaemic
Screen for intracardiac thrombus and arrhythmia, and refer early to a heart failure clinic
Counsel against alcohol and NSAIDs, review salt and fluid intake, and vaccinate against influenza
Discuss prognosis openly and plan close follow up with repeat ejection fraction assessment
management.model: Inpatient decongestion with loop diuretic then stepwise guideline directed heart failure therapy and clinic referral

sources: ESC guideline on heart failure, in own words
ASE chamber quantification guideline, in own words
stem: A 29 year old auto driver from Chennai presents with two months of progressive breathlessness after a dengue like febrile illness, now breathless at rest with ankle oedema. The apex is displaced, a third sound is heard, and the ECG shows left bundle branch block.
teaching: A post viral dilated phenotype after dengue like fever is a common Indian route into severe systolic failure
A displaced diffuse apex plus a third sound gallop means a dilated failing ventricle at the bedside
Ejection fraction below 30 percent with a dilated chamber defines severe disease
Decongest first with a loop diuretic, then build the four pillar heart failure regimen
title: Severe dilated cardiomyopathy after dengue like myocarditis
